pros: High accuracy according to available data
cons: No validation in prospective management outcome studies
Not readily available in all centres
notes: Highest radiation, effective dose 10–20 mSv (footnote b)

content.abbreviations: CTPA = computed tomographic pulmonary angiography; mGy = milligray; mSv = millisieverts; PE = pulmonary embolism; SPECT = single-photon emission computed tomography; V/Q = ventilation/perfusion (lung scintigraphy).

footnotes.a: Effective radiation dose is expressed in mSv (dose in mSv = absorbed dose in mGy × radiation weighting factor (1.0 for X-rays) × tissue weighting factor). Reflects effective doses of all organs exposed (overall radiation dose to the body).
footnotes.b: For comparison, the whole-body effective dose of a chest X-ray examination is 0.1 mSv.

content.section_4_6_summary: The planar ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) lung scintigraphy scan is an established diagnostic test for suspected pulmonary embolism (PE). Perfusion scans are combined with ventilation studies using various tracers. The ventilation scan increases specificity; in acute PE ventilation is expected to be normal in hypoperfused (mismatched) segments.
indications_and_preferred_use: Preferentially applied in outpatients with low clinical probability and a normal chest X-ray
Preferred in patients with history of contrast medium–induced anaphylaxis
Preferred in patients with severe renal failure
content.classification_and_criteria: Planar lung scan results are frequently classified according to the criteria established in the PIOPED study; these criteria have been debated and revised.
